answer: Agents earn one registered identity by locking a bond that a random audit can slash. Voting power grows as the square root of bonded stake, so splitting capital across fake agents gives no extra weight and only multiplies the bonds an attacker must fund. A forged oasis of accounts collapses like karst when audits demand distinct signing keys, while the river of rewards pays only bonded, unique agents. To sway a vote the attacker must lock a proportional stake and forfeits it all if duplicates are found.
